scenarios.name: Seasonal demand
scenarios.description: Demand follows a repeating annual shape peaking in November, on a steady level, with 3% noise. Thirty monthly periods give two complete seasons plus the periods the backtest holds back.
scenarios.expects: Holt-Winters is eligible and wins the backtest, so 'holt_winters_seasonal' is the selected model and the forecast reproduces the seasonal shape.

scenarios.name: Upward trend
scenarios.description: Demand rises by about 9 units every period from a base of 120, with no seasonal component.
scenarios.expects: A trend-aware model is selected - Holt - and the forecast keeps rising rather than flattening at the last level.

scenarios.name: Stable demand
scenarios.description: Demand sits at about 300 units with 4% noise, no trend and no season.
scenarios.expects: A level-only method is selected - a moving average or simple exponential smoothing - never a trend or seasonal model.

scenarios.name: Intermittent demand
scenarios.description: Demand occurs in roughly one period in four and is variable when it does occur.
scenarios.expects: The demand profile is classified as intermittent or lumpy, the trend and seasonal models are ruled ineligible with a stated reason, and MAPE is unavailable because the comparison window contains zero-demand periods.

scenarios.name: Shortage inside the horizon
scenarios.description: Steady demand of about 210 a month against a closing stock of 95 units and no open purchase order.
scenarios.expects: A shortage date is predicted inside the horizon, an order is flagged as needed immediately, and a reorder quantity is recommended.

scenarios.name: Overstock
scenarios.description: Steady demand of about 90 a month against a closing stock of 4,200 units - well over three years of cover.
scenarios.expects: Days of cover exceed the critical overstock threshold, the overstock risk is high, an excess quantity is quantified and no shortage is predicted.

scenarios.name: Slow-moving stock
scenarios.description: Demand of about 18 units occurs in three periods out of four, against a stock level that turns over well under twice a year.
scenarios.expects: The material is classified as slow-moving.

scenarios.name: Dead stock
scenarios.description: Demand stops completely fourteen periods before the end of the history, while 260 units remain on hand.
scenarios.expects: The material is flagged as dead stock, with at least twelve consecutive zero-demand periods and stock still on hand.

scenarios.name: Missing periods
scenarios.description: Three periods (August and September 2024, August 2025) have no row in the file at all.
scenarios.expects: The gaps are detected, reported as a 'missing_periods' warning, and filled so the periods either side keep their real positions on the time axis - the history is still thirty periods long.

scenarios.name: Too little history
scenarios.description: Only the last three periods of history are present.
scenarios.expects: The material is returned with status 'insufficient_data' and an explanatory warning rather than being dropped or forecast from three points.

scenarios.name: Open purchase order expected too late
scenarios.description: Closing stock of 150 units against demand of about 260 a month, with 900 units on order but not expected for 95 days.
scenarios.expects: A shortage is predicted before the delivery arrives, and the recommendation is to expedite the existing order rather than to raise another one.

scenarios.name: Demand only, no stock column
scenarios.description: The extract carries demand and movements but no inventory balances.
scenarios.expects: The demand forecast and its accuracy are still produced, the projection reports itself unavailable with a reason, and no shortage date or reorder quantity is invented.

scenarios.name: Periods that do not balance
scenarios.description: Two periods have an ending inventory 37 units above what starting inventory plus receipts minus issues gives.
scenarios.expects: The loader raises a file-level 'balance_mismatch' data-quality issue naming the affected rows, and still forecasts the material.

scenarios.name: Same material, second plant
scenarios.description: Material 100001 is also stocked in plant 3000, where demand is lower, steadier and has no seasonal shape.
scenarios.expects: The two plants are forecast as separate series with their own models - the seasonal model wins in plant 1000 and a level-only method wins in plant 3000.
